newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to ask for yen coordination at G7 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to ask for yen coordination at G7 - paper.

text.p: Japan will ask other major industrial nations to help curb the sharp fall of the yen against the dollar at this week's Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers meeting in Berlin, a top economic daily said Sunday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, quoting international monetary sources, said Japan plans to ask the other G7 countries -- the United States, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Canada -- to jointly call for stability in currency markets.

Japan's finance ministry has been worried that a weaker yen would reignite U.S.-Japan trade friction after Japan's trade surplus with the U.S. in the last quarter of 1996 showed its first year-on-year rise in almost two years, it said.
A further plunge in the yen may also bring Tokyo stock prices down sharply and put a dent in the nation's economic activity, the paper said.
Tokyo has mostly sounded ambivalent about the recent dollar strength, with monetary officials repeatedly saying only that they oppose wide swings in exchange rates in either direction.
Deputy finance ministers from the G7 are expected to meet on Monday in Frankfurt to discuss the dollar's steep rise, among other issues, international monetary sources said in Washington on Friday.
The meeting is designed to pave the way and set the agenda for the February 8 gathering of finance ministers and central banks chief in Berlin.
